system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Matched-pair MIL ranking: borrowing the ranking objective of weakly supervised video anomaly detection
SUMMARY: Train the segmentation adapters with a ranking loss that requires the most anomalous patches of an abnormal image to score above the most anomalous patches of its most similar normal image from the same dataset, instead of pushing absolute probabilities to 0 and 1.
HYPOTHESIS: A matched-pair hinge ranking loss between the top-k patches of an abnormal image and those of its nearest normal image (CLS similarity, same dataset) yields at least 2 points higher held-out pixel AUROC than top-k BCE MIL, because a relative constraint against matched anatomy does not reward salient normal structures that both images share.
RATIONALE: Weakly supervised video anomaly detection learns frame-level localisation from video-level labels with a MIL ranking loss: the highest-scoring segment of an anomalous video must outrank the highest-scoring segment of a normal video. The analogous principle applies to MVFA's patch maps, with one improvement available in medical data: pairing each abnormal image with the most similar normal image of the same dataset. Anatomy that both images share then cancels in the ranking, so the loss only rewards patches that are anomalous relative to matched normal anatomy — the failure mode that per-image top-k BCE and witness-rate tuning cannot remove.
METHOD: 1) precompute_pairs.py: per source dataset, frozen CLIP CLS embeddings; for each abnormal training image its 5 nearest normal images. 2) loss.py: rank_mil(p_abn, p_nor, k_frac=0.01, margin=0.2) = max(0, margin - topk_mean(p_abn) + topk_mean(p_nor)) + 1e-3 x smoothness (sum of squared differences of neighbouring patches) + 1e-3 x sparsity (mean p_abn), per level as in Sultani et al. 3) train_zero.py: batches contain an abnormal image and one of its matched normals (random among the 5); normal images also receive top-k BCE towards 0. 4) Hyper-parameters: margin {0.1, 0.2, 0.5}; released learning rate and epochs.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: top-k BCE MIL; ranking with random (unmatched) normal pairs. Falsified if matched ranking does not beat top-k BCE MIL, or if unmatched pairs work as well (pairing does not matter).

Idea B:
TITLE: MPE-anchored posterior MIL
SUMMARY: Fix the mixing proportion of the posterior-weighted MIL mixture to the witness rate estimated by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation, and fit only the lesion component, which makes the per-patch posteriors stable early in training while keeping soft targets.
HYPOTHESIS: Anchoring the mixture proportion to the MPE estimate reduces the epoch-to-epoch variation of the fitted lesion posterior by at least 50% and raises held-out AUPRO by at least 1 point over free-proportion posterior MIL.
RATIONALE: The witness-rate parent estimates the proportion of lesion patches robustly but uses it only as a hard k; the posterior parent uses soft targets but must estimate proportion and lesion component jointly, which is unstable when the two distributions overlap early in training. Using the MPE estimate as the fixed proportion and fitting only the lesion component combines the robust part of one with the soft targets of the other.
METHOD: 1) Every 2 epochs per source dataset and level: pi_d from the best-bin MPE estimator; f0 from normal-image patch scores (kernel density); f1 Gaussian fitted by EM with pi fixed to pi_d. 2) Posterior weights as in posterior MIL; weighted BCE for abnormal images; BCE towards 0 for normal images. 3) First 2 epochs: top-k MIL. Hyper-parameters: refit interval 2 epochs; pi clip [0.005, 0.3].
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: posterior MIL with free proportion; witness-rate top-k MIL. Diagnostics: posterior stability across epochs; posterior AUROC against masks on source images. Falsified if AUPRO does not improve over free-proportion posterior MIL.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea A directly addresses the specific pathology of multi-level patch-to-text MIL in medical imaging—namely, that salient normal anatomy erroneously triggers high text-similarity scores across shared modalities—by conditioning ranking on anatomically matched normal reference pairs via frozen CLIP CLS embeddings. In contrast, Idea B relies on an unverified presupposition that unstable mixture-proportion estimation is the core bottleneck and introduces complex, heuristic EM/KDE refitting machinery that does not specifically exploit MVFA's cross-modal vision-language architecture. Furthermore, Idea A's implementation is lightweight, directly testable on a single GPU, and has clean, controlled baselines (including unmatched pairing) to isolate the causal mechanism.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
